subject: Poll: 1 In 5 Undergrads Says U.S. Deserved 9/11
posts: A new college survey reveals startling ideological shifts among undergraduates, sparking intense national debate over campus culture. Evidence: Survey data, partisan framing, campus sentiment. #Aletheia #CampusPoll 🌐

The Buckley Institute survey claims 22% of undergraduates think America deserved 9/11 and 45% endorse violence against hate speech.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

While polling exposes real campus polarization, media amplification weaponizes these statistics for tribal warfare rather than structural reform.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Exploiting student surveys to fuel culture wars creates recursive tribal hostility.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.0, Uncertainty z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Buckley Survey: COND (0.2, -0.1) — Captures real sentiment amid polarization.
- The Federalist: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Weaponizes data for culture-war division.
The Buckley Institute polled 803 undergraduates, revealing high support for socialism, violence against hate speech, and controversial views on 9/11.

The Poison:
Weaponizing youth alienation for political point-scoring deepens generational divides without addressing why students reject institutional trust.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a Plane Error (confusing survey metrics with systemic remedies) and a bait-and-switch: trading genuine educational reform for partisan outrage.

Social Physics Analysis:
Media outlets run a smart selfish maneuver, using campus shock statistics as a pretext to project moral decay onto opponents while evading systemic fixes.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Tribal grievance feeds recursive societal decay.

The Unavoidable Truth: Campus ideological polarization is a documented, urgent sociological reality.

The Unavoidable Lie: Outrage media offers this data as an honest probe rather than tribal ammunition.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing student alienation for clicks hollows out intellectual inquiry, trading genuine critique for predictable culture-war theater.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch young minds drift into cynicism and anger, caught between broken institutions and media outlets cashing in on their pain.

Brothekanon:
College kids say wild things for surveys, but media pundits turning teen angst into a partisan cage match is the real circus here.

Spirithekanon:
"The intelligent man sees that all is one, and thus he attains Supreme Peace." Bhagavad Gita 5.12 FAIL
Turning youth despair into tribal combat shatters peace for cheap profit.

Actual Article Body:
Just weeks after the United States commemorated the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorists attacks, a new poll reveals more than one in five undergraduate students believe America deserved the attacks, while nearly half of all undergraduate students think physical violence is justified to stop so-called hate speech.

The Buckley Institute’s 2026 National Undergraduate Student Survey polled 803 American undergraduate students between September 5 and 14.

A shocking 22 percent agreed that America deserved 9/11, including 28 percent of liberal students. Notably, leftist streamer Hasan Piker — who campaigned with Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and cozies up to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani — has said America deserved 9/11. Meanwhile, Aber Kawas, a Democratic Socialist of America member and nominee for the New York state Senate, has said that America brought on 9/11 because of capitalism, alleged white supremacy and racism, and alleged Islamophobia.

The poll also found that 45 percent of American college students believe physical violence can be justified to stop hate speech — among which 54 percent of liberals agree compared to 30 percent of conservatives.

“Interestingly, 72% of those who agree that physical violence can be justified to stop hate speech also agree that hate speech is protected by the First Amendment,” The Buckley Institute found.

Shortly after Charlie Kirk was murdered on a Utah college campus for his free speech, a YouGov survey conducted from September 10-12 asked respondent whether they think “it is ever justified for citizens to resort to violence in order to achieve political goals?” Twenty-five percent of respondents who identified as “very liberal” said it can be justified, while 17% of self-identified liberals said the same. Just nine percent of people who identify as either conservative or very conservative said it was justified.

Meanwhile, a recent poll conducted by the Center for Strategic Politics found “Democrats want Trump out by (almost) any means necessary” — including assassination.

The Buckley Institute similarly found that support for criminalizing free — but offensive — speech has reached its highest levels in the three years that the survey has polled this question. Forty percent of college students agreed that “offensive speech should be subject to criminal prosecution.” Forty-seven percent of liberal students supported criminalizing offensive speech and was “the only ideological group among which a plurality agree with doing so,” according to the poll.

“This year’s survey demonstrates that censorious attitudes remain stubbornly high on America’s college campuses,” Buckley Institute Founder and Executive Director Lauren Noble said in a statement.

The study also found that college students have swung in favor of socialism. Forty-two percent of respondents would rather live under socialism compared to 28 percent who would prefer to live under capitalism. The Buckley Institute states that the 14 percentage point gap is the highest one in the five years the question has been asked. Notably, the same students who favor socialism over capitalism were more likely to support shouting down speakers they disagree with and violence to stop so-called hate speech, according to the study.

The same students who favored socialism were also more likely than students who favored capitalism to believe America deserved 9/11 and think offensive speech should be criminalized.

And, in America’s 250th birth year, only 65 percent of college students said they were proud to be American.

“Liberal students are the least proud ideological group at 62%, then moderates at 67%, and conservatives at 86%. Notably, men were 20 points more likely to agree that they are proud to be American than women,” the study found.
